messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm working through migrating the old alert rules into the SLO cards UI. Found a few weird edge cases around per-tenant overrides + composite alerts, want quick sanity check before I wire the API.
alex: thanks, what kind of edge cases?
sahil: most common is duplicate notifications when a legacy composite rule expands to multiple sub-rules. we need dedupe at the routing layer or the console should show 'merged' alerts.
maria: exactly. example: legacy rule fires if any of 3 downstream services exceed 5% error. translation creates three child SLO alerts + a parent. If each child keeps original notification list, tenants get 3 identical pings.
jen: +1. also saw owner -> notification_channel mapping differences. old rule had owner=email; new system uses channel IDs. mapping isn't 1:1 for some tenants.
maria: proposal: translation should (1) translate owner -> channel using tenant mapping table, (2) detect identical channel+payloads across siblings and dedupe by creating a single routed notification with a reference to contributing SLOs.
alex: sounds good. question: UI should expose that merged notification so users can edit it inline, right? otherwise they'll be confused why one notification affects multiple SLOs.
maria: yes — console idea: show notification "bundle" with a preview of contributing SLOs and an inline edit that updates the routing policy for all members. also show a translation log entry: original_rule_id -> new_entities.
sahil: technical note: need to preserve escalation policies and rate limits from legacy rules. legacy had cooldowns that are global per-tenant; if we naively translate per-child we'll break rate limits.
jen: can we store original cooldown as metadata and have the router consider it when deduping? e.g., router checks translation_tag and applies legacy_cooldown.
alex: yes, router can check "translation_tag" header. if present, apply legacy cooldown across siblings.
maria: here's a tiny pseudocode translation function I sketched:

```
fn translate_rule(r):
  channels = map_owner_to_channels(r.owner, r.tenant)
  children = expand_composite(r.conditions)
  for c in children:
    create_slo(c, tenant=r.tenant, annotations={ "legacy_id": r.id })
  if identical_notifications(children):
    create_merged_notification(channels, children, cooldown=r.cooldown)
  else:
    attach_individual_notifications(children, channels)
```

sahil: love it. one more: some legacy rules referenced a webhook URL paramized by tenant. translation needs to stash the raw URL in encrypted metadata and only expose a masked preview in the UI.
jen: security + compliance check — store tenant webhook in KMS-wrapped field and show last 4 chars in console.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: migration job started for tenant "acme-corp" (37 rules)
maria: quick ops command I used to find candidates in repo:

`rg "legacy_alert" -n alerts/ | sed -n '1,200p'`

alex: let's also add a small migration dry-run endpoint that returns a mapping preview and potential collisions so customers can opt-in.
sahil: +1, an endpoint like GET /migrate/preview?tenant=... returns list of translations + warnings. include a sample curl in docs.
jen: UX note: show a toggle in SLO card: "show translated from legacy rule". default collapsed.
maria: OK next steps: I will (a) add translation function mock in api repo, (b) wire preview endpoint, (c) add router flag to honor translation cooldowns, (d) add UI card for merged notifications with inline edit and translation log.
alex: timeline? also need brief for support/vue docs.
maria: aim to have API + preview in PR by EOD Thursday. UI sketch Tues. support doc stub Wed.
jen: I can pair on the UI sketch Tue AM.
sahil: I'll own router changes + tests.
maria: thanks all — ping me in thread if you see other odd mappings. leaving a short checklist in the migration PR.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: migration job for "acme-corp" completed (37 rules translated, 5 collisions flagged).
